summary: Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Cambridge and at Birmingham under John Hick (~1981–1985). He taught at West London Institute (~1985–1989) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (1993).

Gavin Flood is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University (~1975–1988) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. His appointments include positions at Lampeter, Oxford (2005–2015), Stirling (~2005–2008), and Yale-NUS College (2016).

Gaya Charan Tripathi is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Ulrich Schneider (~1963–1966). He served as Principal of the Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha from around 1977 to 1999.
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indology scholar affiliated with the University of Tübingen, where she was attested in 2026 as a doctoral student under Claire Maes and as a faculty member.
Geir Heierstad is an Indology scholar who served as Director at Oslo Metropolitan University in 2014 and held a faculty post at the University of Oslo (attested 2026).

Gelek is a scholar in Tibetology. Attested as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center in 1998, Gelek has also served as a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford and a visiting lecturer at the University of California.

Gelek Rimpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Geshe Lharampa at Drepung Monastery, studied at Cornell, and was mentored by Ling and Trijang Rinpoches. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart (1988).

Gembo Dorji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving traditional instruction from teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959, doctorate 1991). He worked as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1964–1974) and served as a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.
Gendun Chopel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries, learning under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
Gendun Chophel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso (~1921–1927). He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Gendun Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, serving as its abbot and retreat master from around 1977 to 1997. He also founded Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, Dhagpo Dargye Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling.

Genjun Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who graduated from Kyoto University. He was a professor at Otani University (attested 1974–1995) and held visiting positions at the University of Hamburg (1956) and Harvard University.
Genro was an 18th-century figure in Buddhist studies who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of head monk (dai-ichiza) at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1931–1934) and later served there as a professor from around 1958 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees including a PhD from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1968–1973) and served at Rissho University (1980–1996), where he became professor emeritus.
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Toyo University and became a dharma heir under Sogaku Harada.
Genzao was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950, receiving traditional instruction from Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a religious studies and Iranian specialist who studied at Stockholm, Copenhagen, and Uppsala, where he earned his PhD under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He served as dean at Uppsala University (1937–1973) and president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Tsetan Chonjore, earned a Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington (1998), held a fellowship at Australian National University, and joined Washington University in St. Louis in 2002.
